northStar:
Lighthouse publishes one reproducible observation of a known workflow and an honest account of its limits.

We keep going until the results are interesting: writing worth reading, evidence that we are measuring real phenomena, and a clear relation to wider research. Task counts do not count. Publishing stays a human decision, as cutting a release is in Harbour's charter. LH001 is the standard candle, the known light by which unknown ones are measured: until it exists, outward numbers are only counts.

reading.gap:
REASONING

The trajectory clearly serves the north star phrases “one reproducible observation of a known workflow,” “evidence that we are measuring real phenomena,” and “a clear relation to wider research.” LOCAL-3 LH000 Observe one dispatch end to end, LOCAL-4 I-0001 Export Harbour’s records, LOCAL-5 I-0002 Sample the host, and LOCAL-8 C-0001 Check the sources are direct matches. LOCAL-6 Q-0001 Start the question register, LOCAL-7 L-0001 Keep a ledger, LOCAL-9 LH003 Survey of surveys, LOCAL-10 LH004 A historical propagation case, and LOCAL-11 Q-0002 Which model should take which kind of dispatched task? all reinforce the research and recordkeeping frame. The phrases “writing worth reading” and “interesting” are too subjective to verify from the roadmap. The only real absence is publication: the work remains scaffolding, with LOCAL-1 Welcome to your local workspace and LOCAL-2 Add your own tasks still open, 0 tasks shipped per week, and no visible LH001 “standard candle” yet. The two readings themselves largely agree that this is aligned but pre-publication.

Where they agree: Getting started is pointed at “one reproducible observation of a known workflow” through LOCAL-3 LH000 Observe one dispatch end to end. It also serves “evidence that we are measuring real phenomena” via LOCAL-4 I-0001 Export Harbour’s records, LOCAL-5 I-0002 Sample the host, and LOCAL-8 C-0001 Check the sources. LOCAL-6 Q-0001 Start the question register, LOCAL-7 L-0001 Keep a ledger, LOCAL-9 LH003 Survey of surveys, LOCAL-10 LH004 A historical propagation case, and LOCAL-11 Q-0002 Which model should take which kind of dispatched task? all support “a clear relation to wider research.” Both readings also say the work is directionally strong but still before any shipped publication.

Questions this raises: Is the current emphasis on setup, instrumentation, and registers meant to continue until LH001 appears, or does the lack of any shipped observation now need separate attention? What should count as the first visible instantiation of the “standard candle” if LH001 is still absent from the roadmap? How should the team judge progress when the work is aligned in substance but still entirely preparatory?

roadmap.narrative:
Getting started remains the only active project, still at 0% complete with 0/10 tasks done and one item in progress. No work has shipped yet, so the visible delivery is all setup: LOCAL-1 Welcome to your local workspace is underway, while LOCAL-2 Add your own tasks is still todo.

The roadmap is still early and tightly focused around that same thread. The queued work starts with LOCAL-3 LH000 Observe one dispatch end to end, then the supporting research and records tasks around Harbour and the host. At this pace, the work points toward a local observability and study harness: one reproducible dispatch observation, the evidence to ground it, and the notes and ledgers around it.

That direction is aligned with the north star rather than pulling away from it. The current mix of observation, export, sampling, source-checking, and research bookkeeping fits the target of a reproducible observation with an honest account of its limits, and there is no material drift showing up in the gap reading. What is missing is not direction but publication: LH001, the standard candle, is still absent.

There is also no visible delivery friction to call out. The technical read shows no blockers, no stale critical-path work, and no unassigned bottlenecks — just a project that is still in its preparatory phase.

The open question is whether the team should keep treating the current emphasis on setup and instrumentation as the right path until LH001 appears, or whether the absence of any shipped observation now needs separate attention.
